title: Gamma SLA-driven pool design and sim runbook
content:
Context:
Customer: Gamma Health — latency-sensitive chat assistant embedded in clinician EHR workflows. Goal: 99th percentile end-to-end response latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens generated), predictable monthly committed spend, and burst tolerance for peak clinic hours.

Current ask / deliverables:
- Small feasibility sim that yields recommended reserved GPU pool size (min commit) for steady-state and burst windows.
- Concrete autoscaling policy (metrics + thresholds + cooldowns) for Dedicated offering.
- Rough monthly committed cost envelope + optional burst-on-demand budget.
- Runbook items for onboarding + observability checks during canary.

Assumptions used in sizing (empirical + conservative):
- Typical request mix: 70% short queries (10-80 tokens generated), 25% medium (80-400 tokens), 5% long (>400).
- Average tokens generated per request (weighted) ~ 96 tokens.
- Average request input tokens ~ 24 tokens.
- End-to-end LLM time dominated by generation step; prefix/cache lookups negligible in this workload.
- Testbed measurements (H100-equivalent on 13B quantized model): generation throughput ~ 6k tokens/sec sustained; effective per-GPU request throughput ~ 55 req/sec for our weighted mix. (This is measured on internal bench; treat as tuning parameter.)
- Target SLO: P99 <= 250ms for short queries (<=128 gen tokens). For medium/long we allow higher tail.

Sizing methodology (practical steps):
1) Baseline steady-state RPS estimate (provided by customer): 120 RPS average during clinic hours, 300 RPS 95th percentile peak. Confirmed via customer logs (sample attached in linked_artifacts).
2) Convert to tokens/sec: 120 req/s * 96 tokens/req = 11,520 tokens/sec sustained.
3) Using bench throughput 6k tokens/sec per GPU -> needed GPUs = ceil(11,520 / 6,000) = 2 GPUs. However this is raw throughput and ignores latency SLO and queueing overhead.
4) SLO headroom multiplier: pick 2.0x for tail-sensitive setups (to minimize batching-induced latency and preserve P99). Effective recommended reserved pool = 4 GPUs for steady-state.
5) Burst sizing: for predictable peaks to 300 RPS -> tokens/sec = 28,800 -> GPUs raw = 5; with SLO headroom, recommended burst capacity = add-on 3 GPUs (so on-demand or warm-burst pool). Final deployed pool config: 4 committed GPUs + 3 burstable (on-demand or warm standby).

Why the headroom multiplier is 2.0x (qualitative):
- Continuous batching yields throughput gains but increases per-request queuing time; for P99 <=250ms we need to keep batching small for short prompts.
- KV cache/warm-start effectiveness varies by convo length; we assume limited cache reuse for clinical pulls.
- Spare GPU capacity reduces model fallback risk and allows for canary/rollout traffic on same pool.

Autoscaling policy (recommended for Dedicated):
- Metrics to drive scale decisions: GPU utilization (dealer-level aggregated), request queue length (pending requests older than 10ms), 95th token queue wait, and a short-term RPS forecast.
- Scale-out rules:
  - Immediate scale-out if 95th-percentile GPU utilization > 82% for 30s OR queue length > 30 requests for 20s.
  - Predictive scale-out: linear forecast over next 60s (EWMA) indicates expected RPS > current capacity * 0.75 for two consecutive windows -> add 1 node.
- Scale-in rules:
  - Only scale-in when 95th-percentile GPU utilization < 35% for 3 minutes AND queue length < 8 for 3 minutes.
  - Minimum committed pool size = 4 (do not scale below committed); scale-in can use burst pool first.
- Cooldowns: 120s between scale events to allow kernels/processes to warm up; prefer incremental single-node adjustments.
- Warm pool / burst strategy:
  - Keep 1 warm standby node (commit reservation + keep container/runtime warm) to cover cold-starts in canary.
  - For customer-requested burst above committed, use on-demand nodes (max 3) for up to 4 hours/day scheduled peaks; if bursts are sustained > 6 hours/day suggest revisiting committed sizing.

Observability knobs and dashboards to add before canary:
- P50/P95/P99 latency by route (short/medium/long) and by model variant.
- Per-GPU token/sec and per-GPU queue length.
- Inflight batch size distribution and batch wait time percentiles.
- Cost exposure: tokens served by committed vs burst nodes, hourly burn.
- Alerts: P99 short-route > 250ms for 5m -> Pager; GPU 95% sustained for 2m -> Page SL; Unexpected fallback to lower model variant -> Pager.

Cost estimate (examples, placeholders to be validated by commercial):
- Committed 4 GPUs (H100-equivalent) — Redwood internal pass-through pricing example: ~$9,600 per GPU/month committed -> 4 * 9,600 = $38,400/month (committed).
- Burstable on-demand nodes (3 nodes, used 30 hours/month) @ $12/hour -> 3 * 30 * 12 = $1,080/month.
- Estimated total month 1 (including buffer, monitoring, early-stage inefficiencies) = ~$40.5k.
Notes: these public numbers are illustrative; finance to provide final quote. If customer needs lower cost target, recommend: increase batching tolerance for non-short routes, push more requests to embeddings or reranking offline, or consider smaller model variants for medium/long queries.

Simulations and quick checks to run during next sync (runbook):
- Run A: replay 2 hours of customer traffic at 95th RPS with current bench image; capture P99 latency distribution and GPU utilization. Produce CSV.
- Run B: stress with synthetic short-only bursts to validate P99 <=250ms with the 4+1 warm pool config.
- Run C: toggle on/off warm pool to measure cold-start tail behavior (container + model load time).

Canary plan (3 stages):
1) Internal limited traffic (10% of clinic sessions, controlled timeframe) on dedicated test pool identical to prod. Validate observability and cost metrics for 48h.
2) Customer-facing canary: route 1 clinic -> measure real-world permutations for 7 days.
3) Ramp to full baseline committed traffic, enable burst policy for scheduled peaks and monitor for 2 weeks.

Open questions / decisions for commercial & infra:
- Which exact GPU SKU will be committed (H100 vs A100)? pricing + perf differ materially.
- Does Gamma want strict hard P99 SLAs or SLOs with penalties? That affects headroom multiplier and recommended committed size.
- Preferred burst hours and billing cadence (daily cap, monthly cap).

Next steps (owners):
- Run bench simulations (Priya) -> deliver CSV + recommended tuned multiplier by 2025-09-22.
- Cost validation with finance (Ethan) -> draft quote for committed 4 GPUs + burst options by 2025-09-26.
- Autoscale policy PR (SRE infra) (Sofia) -> prototype in staging + telemetry hooks by 2025-09-29.
- Customer sync agenda: present sizing, autoscale policy, and canary plan (Liam) -> 2025-10-02.

Appendix (quick heuristics cheat-sheet):
- tokens/sec target -> GPU_count = ceil((RPS * avg_tokens_per_req) / measured_tokens_per_gpu).
- For tail-first customers pick headroom multiplier 1.7x – 2.2x depending on permissible P99.
- Warm pool size = min(1, ceil(0.1 * committed_pool)) for low-latency workloads; increase if cold-start measured > 150ms additional tail.

Notes-to-self: keep narrative concise for customer slide; include graph from Run A in the Confluence page linked above; attach cost spreadsheet (SE-8421).
